concepts.title: Theme as Rudder for Every Scene
concepts.excerpt: Roth, asked what's the most important craft principle in screenwriting, doesn't hesitate: you have to have some thematic about what you're trying to say, that's always going to be underneath it, so that when you have a scene that feels inert that you have to find a way to compare somehow utilize it with the theme of the movie.

concepts.title: Three-Act Shakespearean Discipline
concepts.excerpt: Roth, in the middle of a sprawling craft conversation, slams down a single sentence with unusual force: I don't care what who you are, what you're doing.

concepts.title: Find a Home — Opening and Ending Craft
concepts.excerpt: Roth describes what a good opening does in a phrase the interviewer doesn't initially register as profound: have you start feeling also that you've found a home.

concepts.title: Fanciful (Other Side of the Moon) vs Cartoon
concepts.excerpt: Forrest Gump is not a real person. Roth says it directly: I don't think they're real, the people.

concepts.title: Wallet Method Backstory Craft
concepts.excerpt: Michael Cimino once gave Mickey Rourke a wallet. Inside: a photo of the character's supposed daughter, maybe a saying he liked, an old crumpled phone number.

concepts.title: Villain Craft — Understandable Not Likable
concepts.excerpt: Roth, when asked whether all characters need to be likable, answers fast: No.

concepts.title: Character as Inherited Determinism
concepts.excerpt: Roth is in the middle of a screenplay for Scorsese about the mafia coming to New Orleans in 1890.

concepts.title: Erosion and Page One Every Day
concepts.excerpt: Every morning Eric Roth opens his script and goes back to page one. Not because page one needs work.

concepts.title: Adventure of Creating vs Labor of Revising
concepts.excerpt: Watch Roth describe writing. I love that I get to write. Every day is kind of an adventure.

concepts.title: I Never Had Writer's Block — Energy of Getting to Write
concepts.excerpt: Eric Roth, asked about his daily writing process at 80, drops a sentence almost in passing: I've never had writer's block.

concepts.title: The Middle is a Blob — Discover via Next Three Scenes
concepts.excerpt: Roth knows the beginning of every movie he writes. He knows the ending.

concepts.title: Subtext via the Dream-Rule and the Water Commissioner Trap
concepts.excerpt: Two brothers are sitting at a kitchen table. The first brother says: I'm upset with my mother.

concepts.title: Dialogue Economy — Pacino's One Look and the Shoe-Leather Trap
concepts.excerpt: Roth wrote a monologue for The Insider. A page and a half. He thought it was pretty good.

concepts.title: God Is in the Details — Historical Texture as Craft Foundation
concepts.excerpt: In Sicily, 1870, two mafia families fought for control of the citrus crop.

concepts.title: Environmental Tools — Weather and Time of Day Stops Time
concepts.excerpt: Roth has been writing for sixty years and almost never gets blocked. I never had writer's block.

concepts.title: Unconscious Theme — The Elvis Mitchell Loneliness Observation
concepts.excerpt: Roth has been writing screenplays for sixty years. He's written Forrest Gump, Benjamin Button, Munich, Ali, Killers of the Flower Moon, A Star is Born.

concepts.title: Collaboration as Marriage and the Third Rail
concepts.excerpt: Roth has worked with Spielberg, Scorsese, Fincher, Mann, Affleck, Cooper, Reiner, Russell, Kurosawa.

concepts.title: Authenticity as Cross-Director Consensus — The Affleck Salon Finding
concepts.excerpt: Ben Affleck calls Roth. I want to do a writers' room. They set one up — eight writers, modest pay, Roth as Yoda.

concepts.title: Script as Read Document Not Just Filmed
concepts.excerpt: A screenplay exists twice. Once as the blueprint that gets filmed. Once as the document that gets read by producers, executives, agents, actors, directors deciding whether to make the film at all.

concepts.title: Adaptation as 60 Percent Original
concepts.excerpt: Roth has spent sixty years adapting other people's material. Forrest Gump (novel).

concepts.title: Roth Perennial via Generational Handoff
concepts.excerpt: Asked what makes a film last, Roth doesn't reach for a literary answer.

concepts.title: Karma and Samskaras
concepts.excerpt: Karma is not punishment. That's the first thing to set aside. In Yuvraj Srivastava's account — consistent with classical Vedic frameworks — karma is closer to physics.
